cdb_001: You can recognise it by its hollow trunk, roughly half of it gone, leaning toward the fountain beside it. It stands in the Patio de los Naranjos at the Mezquita-Catedral.
cdb_002: You can recognise it by its rows of orange trees lined up with the columns of the prayer hall next door, linked by shallow water channels. It stands as the Patio de los Naranjos.
cdb_006: You can recognise it by its lopsided form, the surviving half of a tree torn apart by a cyclone, with an electrical box bolted to the trunk. It stands over the Plaza del Cristo de Gracia.
cdb_007: You can recognise it by magenta flowers pushing straight out of the old bark and heavy limbs before any leaves appear, splitting into three arms low down. It stands at the gate of the Cementerio de San Rafael.
cdb_008: You can recognise it by its narrow, single dark column, 26.5 metres tall on a crown only 3.5 metres wide. It stands free of charge outside the ticket gate of the Alcazar de los Reyes Cristianos.
cdb_009: You can recognise it by its unusual height, 27 metres, far taller than a Siberian elm normally grows, among clipped hedges. It stands inside the gardens of the Alcazar de los Reyes Cristianos.
cdb_010: You can recognise it as the only tree on the small square, its branches sweeping down with every shoot tip drooping, leaning slightly toward you. It stands in Plaza del Cardenal Toledo.
cdb_011: You can recognise it by its unusual size for a chinaberry, 24.5 metres tall, throwing a wide ceiling of shade against the old city wall. It stands in the Jardines de la Puerta de Almodovar.
cdb_013: You can recognise it by its fan-shaped leaves, unlike any other tree in the garden, turning uniform gold in late autumn. It stands in the Jardines de la Agricultura, the Jardin de los Patos.
cdb_014: You can recognise them by their fine, drooping green twigs that hiss rather than rustle in the wind, grouped as three against a wall. They stand in Plaza de Jeronimo Paez, by the Archaeological Museum.
cdb_016: You can recognise it by its huge trunk, 4.86 metres round, the thickest in the city's catalogue, and a height of nearly 35 metres. It stands in Parque Celia Mendez, east of the Mezquita.
